suppliers.issues_basis: one row per delivery/supplier issue form submission in GC Form Task Answers, deduped by FormId across pulls; d = min(AnsweredDateTime); supplier = the form's own 'Supplier?' answer canonicalised to a standard supplier name; when the form names no supplier, a text search of all its answers for known supplier names attributes it instead (attribution='text', a heuristic); null when neither finds one, never a fake name
suppliers.note: GetCompliant delivery/supplier issue forms - the only supplier signal the estate produces, and self-reported rather than a measured OTIF. This used to read 'the Mapal supplier feeds fail at fetch', which framed it as a credentials problem waiting to be fixed. It was not: those feeds were Mapal Easilys, the business does not use Easilys (Ross, 27/08/2026), and they have been removed from the pull. There is no delivered-vs-ordered source behind them to unlock.
suppliers.issue_categories_basis: keyword heuristic over each issue's free-text 'Issue?' answer, not an official taxonomy - only the 10-row Gmail 'Supplier Issues' feed has a real Issue Category field; buckets: shortage, damage_quality, wrong_item, temperature, invoice_credit, no_issue_recorded, other

months.coverage_note: the answer feed's history starts 2026-09-29 - nothing before it is in range, so this month is an UNDERCOUNT
month to date - the answer feed reaches 2026-10-19

kr1.basis: one row per delivery/supplier issue form submission in GC Form Task Answers, deduped by FormId, bucketed on the month of its own answer date (min AnsweredDateTime) and attributed to the supplier ANSWERED on the form, falling back to a supplier name found in the free-text issue where the question was left blank. Counts forms RAISED in the month; it says nothing about whether they were closed.
kr1.open_note: The old headline, '292 open', is not published as a KR any more and should not be quoted. It summed OpenDeviationsCount over GC Forms Overview rows, which are FORM VERSIONS, not forms: 96 of the 292 sit on ARCHIVED or DELETED versions (the raw field is 'IsArchieved' - GetCompliant's own misspelling, do not 'fix' it), 96 of them on one version that simultaneously reports 0 deviations raised and 0 forms completed. The live-version total is 196. Closing state also depends on sites closing forms in GetCompliant, which they largely do not.

statements.basis: one statement per closed month, generated by the first bake on or after the 1st: per supplier, the issue forms raised by site and category, every issue's verbatim text, the credit/invoice-flagged rows and the month's issue-free delivery rate (supply.otif). PROVISIONAL until the issue feed reaches the month end, then FINAL. OO3 KR5 scores the day it was generated: by the 3rd 100, by the 10th 50, else 0. A weekly Lynas cut is written each Monday while the Lynas exit is live

broth.basis: one cell per site + check-type + day from GC Scheduled Task Answers, deduped by AnswerID across pulls, averaged if >1 reading landed that day; 'checks_missed' counts non-numeric answers (e.g. 'Not registered on time') separately from checks_missed==checks meaning value is null (no numeric reading that day); event-dated on AnsweredDateTime, never pull_date

factory.basis: one row per refractometer form submission at the factory, from the newest pull of 'Factory Broth Readings' (a whole-sheet copy, so one pull is the full history); score = the reading taken AFTER adding ice, Ross's definition, with the before-ice reading carried alongside for context; event-dated on the form's own Date field, falling back to the submission timestamp when that does not parse OR contradicts it (a date after its own submission, or more than 7 days before it, is a typo), never on pull_date; responses with no after-ice reading are excluded and counted in 'excluded', never scored as zero; 'repeat' marks a batch and product read more than once on the same day - both readings are kept, neither averaged; 'grade' is the reading against its product's after-ice SPEC BAND IN FORCE ON THE READING'S OWN DATE, carried on the row as 'band' (tonkotsu 8-9 to 11/10/2026 (Ross, 27/08/2026), 6-7 from 12/10/2026 (Ross, 12/10/2026), chicken 5-6 (Ross, 27/08/2026); bounds inclusive) - 'in', 'low', 'high', or null for a product with no band, which is never graded or coloured; a reading is never re-graded against a band set after it was taken; 'suspect' is a SEPARATE, much cruder test for keying slips (outside a third to three times the median, e.g. 87 for 8.7), kept apart from the band so a typo is not read as a batch that missed spec - 'grades.out_suspect' counts the overlap

tasks.basis: per scheduled-task instance from GC Scheduled Task Answers, most recent pull only (cross-pull AnswerID dedup isn't reliable here - GetCompliant's auto-generated 'missed' placeholder rows carry no AnswerID; see builder comments); a task counts ON TIME when IsSystemOverdue=false (answered before its DueDateTime) and MISSED when IsSystemOverdue=true (GetCompliant auto-closed it at the deadline with Answer='Not registered on time'); event-dated on DueDateTime - the scheduled day, not pull_date - so the date-range filter slices both the per-site bars/table and the drill-down; deleted rows excluded; drill-down capped at 300 rows per site, most recent due date first (see 'total'/'truncated' per site for anything past the cap)

factory_tasks.basis: per due day, the scheduled GetCompliant tasks at AA Factory1 Limited done on time (IsSystemOverdue false, counted once per task - LocalTaskId + TaskID + DueDateTime, the AnswerID where those are missing - across every pull of 'GC Scheduled Task Answers') and missed (auto-closed, counted from the pull holding most of them for the day); 'holes' are days no pull covers. 'months' is what the verifier stores in ops_daily_aggregates.jsonl (metric 'factory_tasks_month') so a closed month stays scoreable after its pulls are gone

supply.supplier_totals_basis: Same orders as the site table above, grouped by the supplier name Kobas sends. Deliveries counts distinct site+delivery-date combinations, so two orders to one site on one day are one delivery; lines and items are the order email's own Line Items and Items Ordered totals. Scheduled deliveries, not confirmed ones - an order confirmation says a delivery was booked, never that it turned up.
supply.supplier_totals_all_basis: Every order the Kobas Orders feed has ever captured, deduped by Kobas Reference, grouped by supplier: 1871 orders with delivery dates 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-27. NOT A COMPLETE TRADING HISTORY. The feed is a rolling 14-day window over order-confirmation emails, so it knows nothing before its first captured email (2026-08-02); with the longest observed order-to-delivery lead being 12 day(s), deliveries are only fully covered from 2026-08-17 onward, which leaves 4 week(s) that should not be compared like for like with the rest. Scheduled deliveries, not confirmed ones - an order confirmation says a delivery was booked, never that it turned up.

partial_weeks.why: starts before the feed's email coverage does, so orders placed for it were never captured

supply.week_spend_basis: Kobas Orders (daily IMAP parse of Kobas order-confirmation emails, pull_date=2026-10-20): one row per order, deduped by Kobas Reference (latest pull wins), summing the email's own TOTAL for orders whose DELIVERY date falls in the current Mon-Sun week, all venues including franchises. Orders as PLACED - confirmation emails carry no delivered status, so there is no delivered/pending split on this source and none is shown; a cancellation made in Kobas without a re-sent email stays in the total

coverage.basis: distinct suppliers in the Kobas Orders feed vs distinct 'Supplier/Sending Venue' in the weekly outstanding-orders report, matched on the canonical supplier name where one is known

otif.basis: ISSUE-FREE DELIVERY RATE (INDICATIVE) - this is NOT OTIF and must not be labelled as one: nothing here observes whether a delivery was on time, and one delivery can carry several issue forms, so the rate can only ever be a lower bound. deliveries = orders with a delivery date in the month from the Kobas Order Emails feed (deduped by Kobas Reference); issues = supplier issues from GC Form Task Answers whose own answer date falls in the month, deduped by FormId - the identical rows the Supplier Issues tab and the KR1 gauge read, so all three reconcile; deliveries are counted only up to the newest day the issue feed covers (2026-10-19) - one dated later cannot have had an issue filed yet, so it is held back (deliveries_held_back) rather than counted as issue-free, and one dated on a day no pull of the issue feed covers is left out (deliveries_in_feed_holes) for the same reason; rate = max(0, deliveries - issues) / deliveries, and is published ONLY for a supplier-month whose order emails cover the whole month for that supplier. Every other supplier-month carries not_measured saying why, and is excluded from the all-supplier total. Real OTIF needs a source that records what was DELIVERED against what was ORDERED - Mapal Supplier Orders, or a delivery file from Lynas.
otif.note: An issue-free-delivery rate, NOT a measured on-time-in-full: nothing here observes whether a delivery arrived on time or complete, only whether an issue was filed against that supplier in the same month. The earliest issue on record is 2026-09-29 (the answers feed landed 2026-08-13, but each pull reaches back about nine days, so it arrived carrying history). The old note here said issue counts 'only start mid-month' and that August was therefore flattered; that was wrong by eight days in the pessimistic direction. What actually limits August is the DELIVERY side: the Kobas order-email feed starts partway through the month, and on a different day for each supplier, which is why no August supplier is measurable at all. Suppliers with deliveries and no issues show 100%; a supplier-month whose emails do not span the month shows 'not measured' with the reason, never 0%. Issues that name no supplier are excluded from the per-supplier rows and disclosed as unattributed_issues.

price_attribution.basis: Each price change is attributed to the supplier whose pack line moved, by three routes in order of evidence. 'diff': two pack-price exports bracket the change and one Ingredient Id moved by exactly that old->new, so the supplier is read off the export row rather than inferred. 'unique': only one supplier sells that ingredient in that pack. 'price': several do, but exactly one is currently at the old or the new price. Scored against 'diff' as ground truth, the other two are 195/195 and 156/156 correct with 0 disagreements - so an unattributed row is missing coverage, never a wrong name. The report's own Parent ID is NOT usable as a key: it names the parent ingredient, while the export's Ingredient Id names a supplier pack line under it, and the two share no values at all. Rows that could not be attributed are counted by reason and excluded, never bucketed into a supplier called '(none)'.

price_spikes.basis: A spike is one supplier pack line rising by 10% or more in a single weekly report, counted once per line per report and attributed to the supplier whose pack line moved. Month shown is 2026-10, by the date Kobas emailed the report (the first pull that carried it, for reports before 04/09/2026), the same calendar-month rule as KR1. Excluded: a first-ever price ('New'), a move of 100% or more (a pack re-spec or a keying slip, not a price), either side priced 0.00, and any line the pack-price export holds twice for one supplier+category+ingredient+pack, whose price cannot be read off a single record. 0.0% of report rows could be attributed to a named supplier (under the 90% bar this system requires before naming suppliers on a scorecard row); 85 qualifying rise(s) across all 3 report(s) held name no supplier and are disclosed rather than assigned. NOT restricted to recently-ordered ingredients: 'Kobas Orders' is parsed from order-confirmation emails and keeps only per-order totals, so there is no ingredient-level order line to filter on. Every priced ingredient is counted. The emails do carry the lines; widening the parser in daily_export.fetch_kobas_orders is what turns this filter on.

supply.price_supplier_basis: the Weekly Ingredient Price Changes report still carries seven columns - Parent ID, Ingredient Name, Pack Size, Unit Volume, Measurement, Old Price, New Price - and no supplier of its own. Since 16/09/2026 the supplier is reconstructed from the Kobas pack-price export ('Kobas Pack Prices'), which has one line per SUPPLIER PACK carrying Supplier Name, Supplier Code, category and the current price. The obvious key does not work and must not be re-added: the report's Parent ID names the parent INGREDIENT and the export's Ingredient Id names a pack line underneath it, and across 427 Parent IDs and 2,664 Ingredient Ids the two sets share no value at all. Attribution instead runs three routes in order of evidence - see price_attribution.basis - and publishes the rate it achieves. Adding a Supplier column, or the pack line's own id, to the price report in Kobas would make this exact and complete; the bake already prefers the report's own answer the day one appears. Either way this only ever shows suppliers that CHANGED a price, because the report is a log of changes - a supplier holding a steady quote never appears in it.
supply.price_flags_basis: built from EVERY archived pull of the price-changes report, deduped by content into distinct reports and dated by the first pull that carried each - the report is emailed weekly but pulled daily, so pull_date would count one report many times. An item is one PACK of one ingredient (Parent ID + pack size + unit volume + measurement): Parent ID alone is not unique, so keying on it would read two packs as one item bouncing. Each row is a change EVENT and an item can have several in one report, which carries no per-event timestamp - within a report the only ordering is row_num. SETTLED = the item's most recent change was a rise and no later report has changed it again, held at least settled_days, measured to the newest report rather than today so a stale bake cannot inflate it. FLUCTUATING = changed in at least flux_reports distinct reports with at least flux_reversals direction changes. SUSPECT = a move beyond suspect_up/suspect_down, which at that size is a pack or unit re-spec rather than a price, held out of the settled list and never repaired. Neither flag can see a price that never appears in the report, because the report only lists changes

cross_ref.basis: coincidence, NOT causation: every broth deviation (GC Scheduled Task Answers, IsDeviation=true) paired with any supplier issue (GC Form Task Answers, delivery/supplier forms) at the SAME site within +/-3 days by event date; join key is site+date via the hand-built SITE_ALIASES map, since site names differ across systems (e.g. 'Maki SJQ Ltd' vs 'Maki SJQ')

kr2.rule: second fault report on the same asset at the same site within 60 days (reported→reported); re-report while first still open = chaser, not repeat

notes.kr4: per site, as the app reports it: statutory items current or due within 30 days over the site's tracked items. 'No evidence' is an item with no certificate on file (a placeholder date) and never counts as compliant. Sorted worst first. The Overview's KR4 is the Group row's figure, from the app's group counts, not a mean of these rows. Grease-trap servicing, which KR4 leaves out (Ross, 09/10/2026), is still in these figures: the app does not separate it yet (grease_traps)
notes.kr2: rule: second fault report on the same asset at the same site within 60 days (reported→reported); re-report while first still open = chaser, not repeat; 1 chaser report(s) merged into the fault they chase, not counted as repeats. Months before Sep 2026 are zero-filled rows from before the app's fault log existed - shown as 'no log', never as 0, and never used as a baseline
notes.faults: open fault reports in the app's queue, how many have been open more than 14 days, and assets currently marked down, as the app reports them
notes.contractors: per contractor: statutory items assigned, overdue, with no certificate on file, the share of its PPM completions done on time over the last 12 months (blank until the app has logged one against a due date - it counts from 25 Sep 2026), and its newest certificate; in the app's own order. These rows add to 220 items, 12 more than the 208 the register tracks - the app's contractor counts do not reconcile with its register; KR4 uses the register's 208

facilities.basis: read-only, from the M&R Facilities app as of 2026-10-21, pulled 2026-10-21 by builders/refresh_facilities.py into data/ops_command/facilities_ppm.json. rows.text: KR2: Reduce repeat maintenance issues by ≥20%
rows.basis: month-to-date, not yet scored (21 days of data) - 0 so far can still become 1, so it is scored only when the month closes; a repeat before then moves the month to the baseline rule - 0 repeat maintenance issues in Oct 2026 across 19 sites in the Facilities app's fault log - a month with 0 repeat issues scores 100, green (Ross, 15/10/2026), with no baseline needed. rows.text: KR1: Maintain Pork broth density within 8-9
rows.basis: The factory's after-ice band for Tonkotsu Broth CHANGED during October 2026 - 8-9 to 11/10/2026 (Ross, 27/08/2026), 6-7 from 12/10/2026 (Ross, 12/10/2026) - so the month is split at the change and each part is averaged against its own band: 41 reading(s) to 11/10 averaged 7.62 against 8-9, 0.38 outside band; 24 reading(s) from 12/10 averaged 6.54 against 6-7, inside band. The month is scored on the distance outside band weighted by each part's readings, 0.2397 - in a month with one band this is simply its mean against its band - and the value shown is the newest part's mean, under the newer band in force in October 2026. 48 of 65 reading(s) were individually in band, each against the band in force on its own date (73.8%), across 20 production day(s), from 'Factory Broth Readings' as at its own pull 2026-10-20. MONTH TO DATE - the month is not finished, so this figure is still moving. THE SCORE IS ON EACH PART'S MEAN against its own band, which is what each band was agreed against; the in-band percentage is shown beside it because a mean can sit inside band while individual batches miss it in both directions. Readings with no after-ice value, no usable date or a non-numeric value are excluded and never scored as zero, exactly as on the Quality tab. The KR's wording is Matthew's sheet's, verbatim ('KR1: Maintain Pork broth density within 8-9'); the factory band in force this month was moved by Ross, 12/10/2026

repeat.when: a logged month with 0 repeat issues (its value is the count, 0)

scorecard.month_basis: the month picker moves the rows whose KR is a per-month measure. A month still in progress is SCORED only once it holds 7 or more days of the KR's own source data (Ross, 09/10/2026); before that its value is shown with 'MTD', score and RAG are left empty, and the objective percentage leaves the row out. A KR that COUNTS (issues, spikes, closures, disruptions, damaged items) is different, because a count can only rise: it scores 0 as soon as it is already past its last tolerance, and otherwise stays MTD until the month closes - it is never green early. A closed month is always scored. Every month it offers was scored HERE, in the builder, against the same band and the same rule as the default month - the picker chooses between finished answers and computes nothing. A KR with no monthly form does not follow it, and counts towards the default month's objective percentage only: carrying a current-state figure back into an earlier month would invent a history the measurement does not have.
scorecard.basis: one row per KR on the 2026 Operations Input sheet - six objectives, thirty KRs, in the sheet's own order and wording. Every KR scores 100, 80, 50 or 0 from the band table in the builder (scorecard.bands) - or, for OO2 KR2 alone, by the one fixed rule beside it (scorecard.band_rules: a month with 0 repeat issues scores 100, Ross 15/10/2026) - and RAG follows the score: 100 green, 80 or 50 amber, 0 red. A band still marked PROPOSED scores exactly like an agreed one and says so on the row until Matthew confirms it. A KR with no target gets no score, and a KR with no source is grey with its blocker named - that list is the remaining build. An objective's percentage is the mean of the KRs that HAVE a score that month; an unscored KR is left out of the mean and never counted as a zero, which is why each objective also says how many of its five scored. The Operations percentage is the mean of OO2-OO6; OO1 is Finance's and is excluded. Four KRs are typed into the sheet itself and read from it: OO2 KR3, OO3 KR3 and OO4 KR1 from their log tabs, and OO4 KR4 from Finance's % actioned. A month left blank on the sheet is not scored. OO1 KR1-KR5 are read from Finance's management-account summary on the 7th of each month and scored PASS/FAIL on each KR's own target (Ross, 15/10/2026) - SCORES ONLY: no figure behind an OO1 score is published, and OO1 shows no objective percentage. OO2 KR5 is read from the Maintenance Contact List 2026. The Operating KPIs below the scorecard are measurements that are not on Matthew's sheet - they are real and Ross uses them, they are simply not what he is scored on.
